credits: bretth18: generator, firmware glue, investigation and documentation.
Pattern-write, window and key-layer idioms follow VECTOR and Analog BD (repeat98) and Sam Banks' MIT octabam editor tooling; firmware addresses cited from octabam and Play Modes (devilfish707).

presentation.label: EUCLIDEAN TRIGS
presentation.summary: Analog Rytm-style Euclidean sequencer: two pulse generators, rotations and a logic operator write real trigs on an audio track.
presentation.overview: Euclid Seq adds an EUCLID trig mode and turns an audio track's trigs into a Euclidean rhythm, as the Analog Rytm's Euclidean mode does. Two generators (PL1, PL2) spread their pulses evenly over the track's length; RO1 and RO2 rotate each, OP combines them (OR, XOR, AND, SUB) and TRO rotates the result. The module writes ordinary trigs into the pattern, so the stock sequencer plays them with its own tempo, track speed, swing, locks and conditions; it keeps no clock. While EUC is on, the TRIG keys cannot add or remove trigs on that track; holding a trig still edits its parameter locks. The track's LFOs can modulate every setting from LFO SETUP's PMTR list; a modulated track plays the generator's pulses live while its stored trigs stay as set.
highlights: PL1/PL2 pulses, RO1/RO2/TRO rotations and OR/XOR/AND/SUB, per track and pattern
Writes real trigs: stock playback, swing, locks, conditions and bank save
LFO destinations: any track LFO can modulate PL1, PL2, RO1, RO2, TRO or OP; the rhythm moves live
An EUCLID trig mode with its own main-screen panel; FUNC+RIGHT opens the six-dial EUCLID page
Follows PATTERN SCALE length changes; no clock of its own
usage: Hold FUNC and press DOWN until TRIG MODE shows EUCLID (audio tracks). The main screen shows the EUCLID panel.
Press FUNC+RIGHT to open the EUCLID page and YES to turn EUC on. A sets PL1, B PL2, D RO1, E RO2, F TRO and LEVEL the operator; C shows the track length.
Press NO to close the page. The page also opens with RIGHT on TRACK TRIG EDIT's TRIGS row. Press YES on the page again to turn EUC off; the trigs remain as ordinary trigs.
For modulation, open LFO SETUP (FUNC+LFO) and turn PMTR past FX2 to EUC PL1, PL2, RO1, RO2, TRO or OP; DEP sets how far the LFO moves it.

limitations: Deliberate stock-flow changes: TRIG MODE gets a seventh row, EUCLID, on audio tracks; in that mode FUNC+RIGHT opens the EUCLID page instead of shifting trigs in grid recording; RIGHT on TRACK TRIG EDIT's TRIGS row opens the page; with EUC on, the TRIG keys, live recording and the FUNC+LEFT/RIGHT trig shift do not place, remove or move trigs on that track; on MKII in grid recording the trig keys show those trigs purple; the project file gets #EUCLID_SEQ= lines (comments the stock loader skips).

EUC settings are saved with the project (#EUCLID_SEQ= lines) and kept over a power cycle in battery RAM 0x100f9000..0x100fd010; they follow banks and patterns, not Parts, and do not follow pattern or track copy/paste. The EUCLID trig mode is runtime state like the stock trig mode and starts as TRACKS after a reboot.

LFO destinations: LFO SETUP's PMTR continues past FX2 into six EUCLID destinations; the Part stores the LFO's own speed as a stock-safe placeholder and the module keeps the destination in battery RAM 0x100fd100..0x100fd710 and #EUCLID_LFO= project lines. Part reload, copy and paste do not carry it.

A modulated EUC track's pulses are decided per step; added pulses play without locks (unless on a trigless lock trig) and firmware look-ahead (sample preload, slide searches) reads the stored pattern, not the live pulses.
Purple trigs need the MKII panel; MKI trig LEDs stay stock.
Audio tracks only; MIDI tracks are not supported.

Functional MKII reports for the page, purple trigs, blocking and the EUCLID trig mode (VACEUCLID2, VACEUCLID4); saving with the project, RELOAD and a power cycle were reported working on MKII with VACEUCLID5; worst-case chip timing is unmeasured.
Like every DRAM module, the build gives up about 10 MB of sample memory to the platform reserve.

storage.label: DRAM data
storage.conditions: One 16,384-byte settings table for 16 banks x 16 patterns x 8 tracks in battery RAM (0x100f9000..0x100fd010), plus the unit's code in the platform reserve. Exact code totals not yet recorded.

processing.label: ColdFire processing
processing.conditions: Runs only on key and knob events on the UI task, never per step or per sample. Not yet measured.

impact.conditions: Knob turns on the EUCLID page with EUC on: one 64-step regeneration per event.

cpu.rationale: Work happens only on key, knob and length-change events: one pass over at most 64 steps. Nothing runs per step or per sample.

dsp.rationale: No DSP code, tables or buffers; stock DSP processing is unchanged.

memory.rationale: A 16 KB settings table in free battery RAM and a few KB of code in the shared platform reserve; no per-instance copies.

tests.summary: Host gates: the generator matches an independent formulation on 633,984 settings; LFO modulation on 40,000 settings; project-file lines round-trip and malformed lines are ignored. Emulator: 34 scripted checks pass on MKII and MKI panels (page, EUC, blocking, locks, length follow, playback timing, the EUCLID trig mode, FUNC+RIGHT, trig shift) plus project save, reload, battery-RAM power cycle and stock compatibility checks, and LFO destinations, live pulses and stock-safety. Functional MKII reports on VACEUCLID2, VACEUCLID4 and VACEUCLID5 (saving with the project and a power cycle).

license.declaration: Original code, icon and thumbnail by bretth18, MIT. Firmware addresses are cited from public module sources and read from the author's own OS; stock key handlers, strings and icon records are referenced by address, never copied. No Elektron firmware, extracted routines, tables or images are included.

access.location: Audio track: FUNC+UP/DOWN (TRIG MODE) chooses EUCLID; FUNC+RIGHT then opens the EUCLID page. Also RIGHT on TRACK TRIG EDIT's TRIGS row.
steps: Include Euclid Seq in your build and select an audio track.
Hold FUNC and press DOWN until TRIG MODE shows EUCLID; release FUNC.
Press FUNC+RIGHT to open the EUCLID page; press YES to turn EUC on.
Press NO to close the page. In grid recording, FUNC+BANK then RIGHT on the TRIGS row opens it too.
